grade.rationale: The data model and storage API are generally clear, but incomplete document validation, inconsistent safe-loading behavior, incorrect retention semantics, and unstable pagination can produce runtime failures or incorrect operational results.

summary: The implementation is readable and uses sensible serialization and filename safeguards. Four correctness and error-handling issues remain, principally around accepting structurally invalid reports, leaking validation exceptions from LoadSafely, retaining more snapshots than documented, and using mutable offset-based trend cursors. Test coverage is unknown because no coverage evidence was supplied.

grade.rationale: Invalid report graphs can be accepted, retention does not implement the documented cutoff, and pagination can duplicate or omit runs as the collection changes.
The records and helper classes are well organized, but validation rules and storage invariants are incomplete and distributed across callers.
Names and documentation are generally clear, although the documented retention behavior differs from the implementation.
LoadSafely promises status-based handling but can leak exceptions produced by validation, and malformed object graphs may fail later with null-reference errors.
Most logic is deterministic and separable, but direct filesystem and clock-independent cursor behavior need focused boundary and mutation tests; actual coverage is unknown.

findings.title: Deserialization accepts incomplete report graphs
findings.description: Validate checks only the schema fields and three Run properties. System.Text.Json can supply null or default values for missing positional-record properties, so a document with a minimally valid Run can be returned even when Subject, Execution, Observations, Delta, Summary, or their nested collections are absent. Consumers such as the trend builder then dereference these values and can fail with NullReferenceException instead of rejecting the snapshot as corrupt.
findings.recommendation: Validate every required top-level and nested value during deserialization, including non-null collections and objects, allowed enum-like strings, numeric ranges, timestamps, and cross-field invariants. Alternatively, mark required JSON properties explicitly and convert all schema violations into JsonException.

findings.title: LoadSafely can throw for malformed snapshots
findings.description: Validation uses ArgumentException.ThrowIfNullOrWhiteSpace for the run ID, while LoadSafely classifies only JsonException and InvalidDataException as corrupt. A snapshot containing an empty run ID therefore leaks ArgumentException, and a null Run can similarly leak NullReferenceException, contradicting the method's documented non-throwing behavior for corrupt files.
findings.recommendation: Make document validation consistently throw JsonException for malformed serialized content and ensure LoadSafely catches the complete, intentionally bounded set of corruption exceptions. Keep environmental I/O failures distinct if they should remain exceptional.

findings.title: Prune retains more unpinned snapshots than documented
findings.description: The documented policy is the newest keep snapshots plus every pinned baseline, but the implementation removes pinned reports before selecting the newest keep entries. If pinned reports occur within the newest keep snapshots, it retains keep unpinned reports in addition to them, preserving older unpinned snapshots that should fall outside the cutoff.
findings.recommendation: Order all reports first, take the newest keep reports, union that set with pinned reports, and delete everything outside the union. Add tests where zero, some, and all of the newest reports are pinned.

findings.title: Offset cursor can skip or duplicate trend entries
findings.description: The cursor is a numeric offset into a series ordered by mutable report data. If a new run is inserted, a run is removed, or a revision changes ordering between page requests, the same offset can repeat an already returned run or skip one that has not been returned.
findings.recommendation: Use an opaque keyset cursor containing the last point's complete deterministic sort key, such as FinishedAt and RunId, and fetch records strictly after that key. Version or sign the cursor if it is part of a public API.
